title: [Arachnoid web presenting as tetraparesis].
summary: Arachnoid webs are rare intradural lesions which disrupt cerebrospinal fluid flow and may cause spinal cord compression. This is a case report of a previously healthy 19-year-old woman who presented with acute back pain and rapidly progressive tetraparesis. MRI revealed cervical spinal cord ischaemia and an arachnoid web at the thoracic level. Surgical removal led to partial neurological recovery. Early recognition is essential, as timely surgery may prevent irreversible injury.

summary: The therapeutic mechanisms of brain-computer interface (BCI) rehabilitation remain partially understood. This study aimed to deconstruct the BCI paradigm to isolate the specific contributions of these core components to functional recovery and cortical reorganization in subacute stroke. title: Lower fibrinogen and fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio in migraine with white matter hyperintensities: implications for microvascular vulnerability.
summary: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are increasingly recognized as imaging markers of migraine-related cerebral small-vessel injury. title: Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient.
summary: Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement. We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. title: Efficacy and safety of tolebrutinib in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
summary: Tolebrutinib is an oral, brain-penetrant Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor being investigated for multiple sclerosis (MS). This systematic review and meta-analysis bring together the available evidence on its clinical efficacy and adverse events. title: Craniovertebral junction injuries in children: a single center retrospective review.
summary: The craniovertebral junction is a unique structure consisting of the occipito-atlantal and atlanto-axial joints and their associated ligaments. title: Genetic architecture of MRI-derived cervical spinal cord morphology reveals sensory-motor axis and systemic disease associations.
summary: The spinal cord is critical to motor, sensory, autonomic function, and increasingly implicated in neurological disease and human health, yet its genetic architecture remains largely unexplored. title: Brain functional changes of suicidal ideation and behaviours: a meta-analysis of task-based fMRI studies.
summary: Suicidal ideation and behaviour are major global mental health issues and leading causes for mortality. summary: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). title: Altered intrinsic neural timescales in cocaine use disorder.
summary: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is a major public health challenge, but its neurodynamic and molecular mechanisms remain unclear despite evidence of structural and functional abnormalities. title: Should I "stay" or should I "go"? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking.
summary: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
summary: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety.
summary: Anxiety comprises partially dissociable cognitive and somatic components, yet it remains unclear whether brief interventions modulate these systems in parallel. title: Sleep underestimation and subjective sleep appraisal: Limited value of routine polysomnographic and electroencephalographic features.
summary: Whether routine polysomnographic (PSG) and electroencephalographic (EEG) features distinguish patients who underestimate sleep remains unclear. title: Action-related brain dynamics during leader-follower coordination

summary: Recent advances in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology have brought speech neuroprostheses closer to restoring naturalistic communication for individuals with severe motor or speech impairments. summary: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, continuously adapting to internal and external signals across rapid and protracted timescales. title: Adolescent prodromal phenotypes of psychiatric disorders: insights from a novel DISC1-perturbed monkey model
summary: Neurodevelopmental deficits frequently lead to mild but significant adolescent social and cognitive changes, representing prodromal manifestations of adult-onset psychiatric disorders in a cross-disease manner. summary: Introduction: Cognitive intraindividual variability (IIV), a measure of fluctuation in performance across time or tasks, is an emerging marker of cognitive decline. title: TriRouter: Sparse-to-Dense Electrode-Space Routing for Robust EEG Motor Imagery Decoding

title: EEG Lempel-Ziv Complexity vis-à-vis Autocorrelation Function
